blocks.body: # La Cajita: production cost and margin

## Executive Summary

- **The planning case leaves about 38% before fixed overhead.** At $17.50 standard, modeled cost is $10.78 and contribution is $6.72 per box. At $19.50 preset printed, modeled cost is $11.98 and contribution is $7.52.
- **This is not verified net profit.** Recipe quantities, batch yields, production time and several packaging costs remain assumptions. The six-component box includes the full salad and dessert.
- **Labor efficiency changes the answer substantially.** Standard-box contribution ranges from 14% to 53% across the illustrated scenarios—not a statistical confidence interval.
- **Consider $18 standard / $20 preset printed as a provisional alternative.** Those prices reach approximately 40% contribution in the planning case. No website prices were changed.

## Count the full production cost, including your own time

This analysis is for one paid order of 25 identical Cajitas, in US dollars, prepared September 9, 2026. The proposed selling prices exclude tax and delivery. Contribution margin equals (selling price − food − waste − packaging − direct labor − variable utilities − payment fees) ÷ selling price. It is **not net profit**. Rent, insurance, equipment, marketing, general administration, delivery and income tax are excluded.

The standard contents are a Hawaiian roll with ham spread, guava-and-cheese empanada, ham croqueta without butter, 6 oz cold salad, one five-ingredient skewer, and 3–4 oz tres leches. The dessert is included even though the event photo omitted it.

## Labor is the largest modeled expense

The planning case assumes 12 staff-minutes per box at a $24 loaded hourly cost—five staff-hours for 25 boxes. This includes allocated prep, assembly, labeling, shopping and cleanup; unattended chilling is not counted as staffed work. The following chart shows estimated dollars per standard box, not observed expenses. Labor is $4.80, compared with $2.72 in ingredients and $2.20 in packaging.

A preset-printed box adds an assumed two minutes of work and $0.35 in materials. Bespoke artwork or oversized boxes could cost more and are not covered by that allowance.

## The food calculation is a recipe proxy, not a kitchen specification

Ingredient-only estimates per box are $0.67 for the roll and ham spread, $0.22 for the empanada, $0.28 for the croqueta, $0.69 for salad, $0.40 for the skewer and $0.45 for tres leches. Frying/seasoning allowances are included in the two fried items.

The salad follows the owner's ingredient list, but to-taste amounts and finished yield are assumed: a $13.88 batch yielding twenty 6 oz portions. The dessert proxy totals $9.07 and assumes twenty cups; actual cup yield has not been measured. The other recipe ratios are costing assumptions, not instructions to alter the products. Buying prepared components instead of making them could materially increase cost.

Retail benchmarks have been refreshed, but no store was pinned to the owner's ZIP code. Brand, promotion, edible yield and purchasing channel can change these amounts. The model therefore stresses ingredients by +30% in the higher-cost case.

## Slower production can absorb most of the cushion

The table compares six planning scenarios at unchanged selling prices. Efficient production assumes 8 minutes at $22/hour; the planning case uses 12 minutes at $24; higher-cost production uses 16 minutes at $28, higher ingredient and packaging costs, and more waste. Printed boxes add two minutes in every scenario. These are operational sensitivity tests—not guaranteed minimum or maximum margins.

The standard higher-cost case leaves only $2.43 per box before fixed overhead. Avoid committing to aggressive discounts until a timed production run confirms the planning case.

## Fixed overhead still has to be paid

For 25 boxes, planning-case contribution is approximately $168 standard or $188 printed. That amount is available to cover fixed costs and profit; it is not take-home pay. If fixed overhead were $1.50 per box, remaining margin would be approximately 29.9% standard or 30.9% printed. That $1.50 is an illustration, not Añejo's measured overhead.

Each extra minute at the assumed $24 hourly cost adds $0.40 per box. The payment model allocates the $0.30 transaction fee across the entire order, rather than charging it to every box. Fees on any collected tax or delivery charge are not included.

## Validate one batch before locking in the price

1. Weigh ingredients and count finished portions from one normal batch; record leftovers separately from waste.
2. Log total staff-hours across all workers, including your time, prep, labels and cleanup.
3. Count both wet-food containers, liners, labels, tags, picks and bags used. The $9.99 dessert-container pack count remains unknown; the $15 printing receipt covered both boxes and trays.
4. Replace the model's allowances with receipts and measured yields, then approve the public prices. $18/$20 provides approximately a 40% planning-case contribution, but $17.50/$19.50 remains a possible lower-price choice if the measured results support it.

The website and draft pricing engine have not been changed by this analysis.

## The most useful missing input is total staff-hours

How many total staff-hours does a 25-Cajita batch take, counting everyone who helps? Also confirm whether empanadas and croquetas are made from scratch or purchased prepared. Receipts and the number of finished portions from each recipe will turn this estimate into an actual cost model.

## What is confirmed—and what remains estimated

Confirmed by the owner: portions, default flavors, six standard components, box replacement cost, and receipt pack prices. Assumed: most recipe ratios/yields, two paper liners, wet-food cups at $0.25 each, $0.40 printing allocation, $0.25 bag/twine/cutlery, 7% food waste, $0.35 variable utilities and loaded labor. Those assumptions are explicitly recorded in the companion calculation.

The BLS reference is a broad May 2024 Miami-metro food-service wage benchmark, not a September 2026 employment quote; $24/hour is an independent loaded-cost assumption. Square's API rate is a public benchmark, not a verified Añejo contract. Packaging purchase tax, shipping and any unallocated costs may raise actual costs. Stock availability, packaging fit and production capacity were not assessed here.
